Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

manimR 0.1.0

  • First release: a native R port of Manim Community 0.22 (the Cairo style renderer), covering every public name and class method of from manim import * (checked by tests/testthat/test-api-coverage.R). Every upstream class has an R6 generator FooClass, including the ones upstream defines only to preset arguments.
  • Rendered output and the LaTeX cache go to a media folder in the R session’s temporary directory unless media_dir is set, so nothing is written to the working directory by default; manim_cli() writes to a media folder in tools::R_user_dir("manimR", "cache") unless --media_dir is given (--media_dir media writes ./media as Manim’s command line does).
  • Output follows Manim 0.22’s render sessions: format is "auto", "mp4", "mov", "webm", "gif", "png" (last frame), "png-sequence" or "none", with dry_run, directory templates (get_dir()), manim.cfg files (digest_config_file()), encoder settings and per scene log files. Partial movie files are cached by a hash of each play, and sections, sound and subtitles are written as upstream.
  • Tex() and MathTex() through LaTeX and dvisvgm, Typst() and MathTypst() through the typst compiler, Text() and MarkupText() through system fonts, and Code() highlighted with Pygments when Python has it.
  • The command line (manim_cli()) takes manim render’s options and the checkhealth, cfg, init, plugins and cache clear subcommands.
  • RStudio addins (including rendering as a background job), a manim knitr engine for R Markdown and Quarto, printing of render() results in documents, Shiny output functions (manimOutput(), renderManim()) and an interactive Shiny window for scenes.
  • as_mobject() turns ggplot2, grid and base graphics into mobjects, scene_frame() renders one frame of a scene, expect_snapshot_frame() tests frames with testthat, and GraphClass$from_igraph() imports igraph graphs.
  • The mobject classes of upstream’s OpenGL renderer (OpenGLCircle(), OpenGLVGroup(), OpenGLSurface() and the rest) build on their Cairo counterparts, so code written for that renderer runs unchanged; OpenGLSurfaceMesh() and OpenGLTexturedSurface() are ported to grid. They also have the methods and argument names of upstream’s OpenGL classes, including the CPU side of its GPU pipeline: shader data, triangulation, uniforms and ShaderWrapper(), with upstream’s GLSL files. The CPU side of upstream’s OpenGL renderer is ported too: the camera (OpenGLCamera()), trees of 3D objects and meshes (Object3D(), Mesh()), Shader(), triangulate_mobject() and build_matrix_lists(). A scene draws meshes whose shader is one of upstream’s default, manim_coords, vertex_colors or test folders in software, and runs the vertex and fragment shaders of other meshes (and FullScreenQuad()) in a GLSL interpreter, structs, geometry shaders and sampler2D textures of the software context included (texture(), textureLod(), texelFetch(), textureSize()); other sampler types and units with no texture read (0, 0, 0, 1), as a GPU’s default texture, since upstream binds only 2D textures. Textures that the renderer makes from images are clamped and sampled at the nearest texel, as upstream’s. OpenGLRenderer() renders scenes (also with manim_config(renderer = "opengl")) through a software context (OpenGLSoftwareContext()) whose framebuffers are ragg devices, the render_opengl_vectorized_mobject_fill() and _stroke() functions draw upstream’s projection shaders by their GLSL rules, and Window() shows a live preview in an R graphics device. Where the device reports no mouse or key events (as on macOS), the window opens in the browser through httpuv and reports pyglet’s events, wheel and key releases included. Surface normals are computed in single precision as on the GPU, so a sphere’s pole takes the shader’s fallback normal where upstream’s does. Where an OpenGL class differs from its Cairo counterpart, it follows upstream’s OpenGL class: OpenGLArrow() is a filled shape, OpenGLLine() applies buff twice, arcs are made of quadratic pieces, add_tip() adds an OpenGLArrowTip(), OpenGLSurface() counts resolution in grid points, and OpenGLArc(), OpenGLCircle(), OpenGLRectangle(), OpenGLImageMobject() and others take upstream’s arguments in upstream’s order, and OpenGLImageMobject() upscales an image array with Pillow’s resampling filters as upstream does. Shapes built under manim_config(renderer = "opengl") follow upstream’s OpenGL constructions: a line is one straight quadratic, a cubic (from an SVG path, add_cubic_bezier_curve_to() or make_smooth()) is two quadratics, MathTex() and Typst() split sharp curves and drop null ones, ThreeDAxes() adds no shaded pieces, group bounds use the quadratic curves, and an empty group keeps track of its shifts. Under that renderer a partial curve keeps its number of curves, and copies added to align groups in a transform stay visible when opaque, as in upstream’s OpenGL mobjects. Mobjects of the classes upstream converts to OpenGL classes under that renderer (all but a bare VMobject() or Mobject(), StreamLine, images and user classes made directly on VMobjectClass or MobjectClass) also get the methods of upstream’s OpenGL classes. Their quadratic curves are stored raised to cubics, so $points and the point getters give 4 points per curve where upstream gives 3.
  • Images are drawn as upstream’s Cairo camera draws them: the truncated pixel corners give the paste box, and the image goes through Pillow’s perspective transform (its nearest, bilinear and bicubic filters on premultiplied 8 bit colors), so frames match upstream’s within 1 of 255. An image seen edge on is skipped as upstream.
  • Helpers of manim.utils outside from manim import * are exported too: the matrices of manim.utils.opengl (orthographic_projection_matrix(), view_matrix() and the rest), rotation_matrix_transpose(), rotation_matrix_from_quaternion(), normalize_along_axis(), resize_array(), resize_preserving_order(), resize_with_interpolation(), batch_by_property(), uniq_chain(), get_smooth_closed_cubic_bezier_handle_points(), get_smooth_open_cubic_bezier_handle_points(), get_quadratic_approximation_of_cubic(), remove_invisible_chars() and convert_audio().
  • ImplicitFunction() traces its curve with a port of the adaptive quadtree of the isosurfaces package, and ConvexHull() and ConvexHull3D() use a port of upstream’s QuickHull, so both give upstream’s curve points and hull faces.
  • Submobjects are validated and inserted as upstream: a VMobject takes only VMobjects, add(), add_to_back() and insert() move a mobject that is already a submobject, and insert() takes negative positions.
  • A numeric vector of 3 or 4 values is one color wherever a color is taken (Square(color = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5))), and a single number is a hex number (0xFC6255); several colors are a character vector or a list.
  • frame_width, frame_height and frame_center of a camera are properties: on a MovingCamera they read and move its frame.
  • SVGMobject() reads styles and paths as upstream’s SVG parser does: a shape with no stroke keeps the stroke color of its class, an opacity property replaces the alpha of its color and has 8 bits, the opacity property is not read, and an arc becomes one quadratic piece for every tenth of a turn. MarkupText() rejects unknown tags, and polylabel() also returns the size h of the cell of its pole.
